claims.text: Purpose: routine prenatal testing checks for anemia, proteinuria, and infections that may affect fetal development or maternal health.
claims.quote: Routine testing evaluates for anemia, proteinuria, and infectious diseases that may affect fetal development or maternal health.

claims.text: First visit: CBC; blood type and alloantibody screen; rubella and varicella immunity; hepatitis C; hepatitis B; HIV; syphilis; gonorrhea and chlamydia; tuberculosis if at risk; urine culture.
claims.quote: CBC X Repeat at 24 to 28 weeks Blood type and screen for alloantibodies X Repeat in patients with Rh-negative blood type at 28 weeks* Rubella and varicella immunity X† Hepatitis C X Hepatitis B X Repeat in high-risk patients at 24 to 28 weeks Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) X Repeat in high-risk patients at 28 to 36 weeks Syphilis X Repeat in high-risk patients at 28 to 36 weeks Gonorrhea and chlamydia X Repeat in high-risk patients at 28 to 36 weeks Tuberculosis (if at risk) X Urine culture X
claims.locator: Table: Components of Routine Prenatal Care, first visit column

claims.text: Repeats: CBC at 24 to 28 weeks; antibody screen at 28 weeks if Rh-negative. In high-risk patients: hepatitis B at 24 to 28 weeks; HIV, syphilis, and gonorrhea and chlamydia at 28 to 36 weeks.
claims.quote: CBC X Repeat at 24 to 28 weeks Blood type and screen for alloantibodies X Repeat in patients with Rh-negative blood type at 28 weeks* Rubella and varicella immunity X† Hepatitis C X Hepatitis B X Repeat in high-risk patients at 24 to 28 weeks Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) X Repeat in high-risk patients at 28 to 36 weeks Syphilis X Repeat in high-risk patients at 28 to 36 weeks Gonorrhea and chlamydia X Repeat in high-risk patients at 28 to 36 weeks
claims.locator: Table: Components of Routine Prenatal Care, repeat column

claims.text: Rh-negative: anti-D immune globulin at 28 weeks, or at 28 and 34 weeks, to prevent alloimmunization.
claims.quote: To prevent alloimmunization, pregnant patients with a Rh-negative blood type should receive anti-D immune globulin injection at either 28 weeks or 28 and 34 weeks.

claims.text: Group B strep: vaginal and rectal swab for GBS colonization at 36 to 37 weeks.
claims.quote: Swab of vagina and rectum for Group B beta-hemolytic streptococcus (GBS) colonization At 36 to 37 weeks‡
claims.locator: Table: Components of Routine Prenatal Care

claims.text: GBS in urine: any colony count at any time in pregnancy means antibiotic prophylaxis at delivery.
claims.quote: Patients with any colony count of Group B streptococcus (GBS) in a urine culture at any time during pregnancy (which suggests heavy vaginal–rectal colonization) should be given antibiotic prophylaxis at the time of delivery

claims.text: Aneuploidy: ACOG recommends offering testing to all women regardless of age or baseline risk, including cell-free DNA (NIPT).
claims.quote: The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists recommends that all women be offered diagnostic testing, irrespective of baseline risk or maternal age, including non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) or cell free DNA testing

claims.locator: Table: Components of Routine Prenatal Care
